title: [WT-09] Wrappers: completion landing with a remote: fetch, push first, retry
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 (L4 with a remote, L9), §2.3 and §2.4 (no-remote behaviour).

Objective: with an origin, the remote's target is updated before the local one by a plain (never forced) push of a commit whose only parent is B, so a lander that lost the race retries instead of diverging.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- sync_land_target / Sync-MoeLandTarget:
  - `git fetch origin refs/heads/<target>`;
  - local equal to or ahead of the fetched tip: B = local;
  - local behind: a CAS fast-forward of the local target, then B = fetched;
  - neither: MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED and nothing moves (record failed for now; WT-11 adds the route);
  - a fetch failure prints MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and B = local;
  - it is also called before WT-04's W creation, so W is cut from a fresh target.
- L9: `git push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/<target>` with no force flag of any kind.
  - A '!' (rejected) line retries from L4 (3 attempts total).
  - A transport failure prints the existing PUSH FAILED banner with code MOE_PUSH_FAILED and continues to the local CAS.
  - MOE_PUSH_REBASE is ignored in worktree mode.
- With no remote, the fetch and push are skipped.
- Register scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh in the Linux postflight job and worktree-landing.ps1 in the Windows jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml.

The WT-08T files (task-c12f9463b68c44a18cc460a7e9460247) are held out: ALL their cases, local and remote, must pass with no edit to them. Depends on WT-08 (task-7a4aab5e0bfa48e0978eb76506edfd57).

NOT in scope: the gate and lease (WT-10); the unlanded route (WT-11); checkpoint pushes (WT-07); board ref pushes (WT-12); docs (WT-18).

Verification: bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1)
definitionOfDone: bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh (all cases) exits 0 with scripts/tests/worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} byte-identical to WT-08T's landed version.
The ps1 twin passes all cases on a Windows seat.
grep over the worktree arm of both wrappers finds no `--force`, `-f ` or `--force-with-lease` on any push; MOE_PUSH_REBASE has no effect in worktree mode (a case or grep proves it).
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs worktree-landing.sh on Linux and worktree-landing.ps1 on Windows.
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh exit 0; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes.

implementationPlan.description:
PREREQUISITES, then the sh L4 remote arm, the mirror helper and the remote W base.

dependsOn gates the claim, not the bytes. Confirm that WT-08 (task-7a4aab5e), WT-08T (task-c12f9463) and WT-04..WT-07 have landed: epicSiblings landing.merged, or `git log --grep 'Moe-Task: <id>'`.

Read before editing:
- the revised docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.2, §2.2 (L4, L9, L10, L12), §2.3 and §2.6;
- this row's two contract comments. They override the description: in remote mode B is never local, there is no local-CAS fallback, and a transport failure never publishes;
- WT-08's landed worktree arm of run_landing / Invoke-MoeLanding: its round loop, how it computes B, its interim failure path for MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT, its L8 journal and its L12;
- WT-04's W creation arm;
- the held-out scripts/tests/worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}: the remote cases and their git shim (MOE_TEST_GIT_FAIL).
Then run `bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh --only remote` on a HEAD snapshot and keep the red baseline. Never edit the held-out files.

scripts/moe-agent.sh:

sync_land_target TARGET (doc L4). If WT-08 inlined its local B computation, move it in here.
- Local mode (no_git_remote): B = the local target, as WT-08 does.
- Remote mode is anything else, including a failed probe:
  - Read L, the local target's tip, BEFORE fetching. L may be absent.
  - Fetch: `git -C "$MOE_TOP" fetch --no-write-fetch-head origin "refs/heads/$target:refs/remotes/origin/$target"`. No '+' and no --force.
  - Up to 3 tries, sleeping MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC between them (default 5; a non-integer or negative value means 5).
  - Call git by name through PATH: WT-08T's shim intercepts it.
  - B = refs/remotes/origin/<target>, never the local target.
  - All 3 tries fail (a refused non-fast-forward counts as a try): print MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED with git's last stderr line, then end the landing through WT-08's interim failure path (record_commit failed, reason remote). Nothing is published and no ref moves.
  - L is present and not an ancestor of B (merge-base --is-ancestor exits 1): MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED, through the same interim path (reason diverged). Nothing moves. Any exit code other than 0 or 1 is a failure, never 'diverged'.
  - Otherwise mirror the local target to B.

mirror_land_target NEW (doc L10's rule; L4, L10 and replay all reuse it):
- `git update-ref refs/heads/<target> NEW <old>`, only while <old> is absent or an ancestor of NEW.
- After a lost CAS, re-read <old> and retry, at most 3 times.
- A target that already contains NEW needs nothing.
- A target that cannot fast-forward prints MOE_LAND_MIRROR_SKIPPED and returns 0. It is never a landing failure.
- WT-08's MOE_LAND_TARGET_CHECKED_OUT check still runs first.

W base (§1.2, in WT-04's creation arm):
- Remote mode: run sync_land_target's fetch part once, with no mirror and no divergence check, then cut W from refs/remotes/origin/<target>.
- If that fetch fails, cut from the ref as last fetched.
- If no such ref exists: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED through WT-04's failure path (no CLI, report_blocked).
- Local mode keeps WT-04's local-target base.

Error handling: check every git exit code, keep stderr to one bounded log line, and never move a ref after a failed or ambiguous answer.

The sh remote publication, inside WT-08's round (L9-L12) and the replay.

L9:
- Push with `git -C "$MOE_TOP" push --porcelain origin "$C:refs/heads/$target"`.
- Never use --force, -f, --force-with-lease or a '+' refspec.
- Never call push_branch, so neither MOE_PUSH_REBASE nor the pull --rebase retry can run in worktree mode.
- Parse the porcelain line whose destination is refs/heads/<target>, whatever git's exit code:
  - flag ' ', '*' or '=': published;
  - '!': rejected. The round ends and the next round starts again at L4 on the fresh tip;
  - anything else (another flag, no line, a transport error): reconcile_push.

reconcile_push C (doc §2.6):
- Sleep MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC, then repeat L4's fetch (3 tries).
- refs/remotes/origin/<target> contains C: published; continue at L10.
- Fetched without C: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, and the round ends.
- Fetch failed: the outcome is unknown.
  - Print MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and move no ref.
  - Rewrite the L8 journal with pushResult 'push unknown: <one-line detail>'.
  - Put C on a rescue ref with reason push-unknown (rescue_ref).
  - Send no completion record_commit and no finalize_attempt, so the attempt stays finalizing.
  - End the landing; no further rounds.

After a confirmed publication:
- L10: mirror_land_target C.
- Then WT-08's L11 and L12, with pushed: true and a journal and receipt pushResult that starts with 'pushed ' (receipt_ledger_send's vocabulary).
- Local mode keeps WT-08's pushed: false.

Rounds (doc §2.3):
- Running out of rounds prints MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION and takes WT-08's interim failure path.
- Reason contention, or remote when the last round ended on MOE_PUSH_FAILED.
- WT-11 replaces the interim path with the unlanded route. Do not call finalize_attempt unlanded here.

receipt_replay worktree arm (doc §2.6):
- Mark a journal written by a worktree-mode remote landing at L8 with one optional field (e.g. landMode). receipt_journal_fields must tolerate its absence, and a journal without it keeps today's arm byte for byte (rail 4).
- For a marked journal, fetch first (L4's fetch, 3 tries). A failed fetch keeps the journal.
- Then run the unchanged receipt_landed_as against refs/remotes/origin/<target>.
- Contained: mirror_land_target to the found commit, then today's owed-row, receipt and finalize-landed steps.
- Fetched but absent: drop the journal as today and log the still-finalizing attempt id. Re-landing it in W belongs to WT-11 (comment-c2d608e0 on task-dd1ee586).

Error handling: an ambiguous push or fetch answer never publishes, never mirrors and never finalizes. Only a confirmed publication sends pushed: true.

The ps1 twin of step 1, in scripts/moe-agent.ps1:
- Sync-MoeLandTarget.
- The mirror helper, named Update-MoeLandTargetMirror (or the Verb-Moe name WT-08 already uses).
- The remote W base in WT-04's ps1 creation arm.

Use the same codes, strings, tries and backoff (MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC, default 5). Run git through Invoke-MoeGit and PATH so WT-08T's shim intercepts it. Compare strings ordinally ([string]::Equals with Ordinal, -ceq for literal refs; mem:gotcha-powershell-path-comparison-culture). Keep the file UTF-8 with a BOM.

Error handling, as in step 1: check every exit code, keep stderr to one bounded line, and move no ref on a failed or ambiguous answer.

Tests and CI.

scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1: add one remote-base arm to each. Reuse WT-04's worktree-arm setup (the fake proxy's workspace, worktreeMode on) and add a bare origin. Cases:
- origin's target is one commit ahead of the local target: W's task branch starts at refs/remotes/origin/<target>. Assert the branch's base commit equals origin's tip, not the local one.
- a remote is configured but unreachable and refs/remotes/origin/<target> does not exist: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, no CLI launched, report_blocked sent, and no W registered.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:
- add `bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh` to 'Test Bash wrapper postflight and parity' (Linux);
- add `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1` to 'Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight';
- add `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1` to 'Test PowerShell 7 wrapper postflight and parity';
- on Windows, follow each new command with the existing `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }` pattern.

Do not edit scripts/tests/worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}.

Budget for the whole task: at most 380 net non-board LOC. Each wrapper gets at most +150, each postflight harness at most +35, and ci.yml at most +10. The 400 review cap counts tests. If honest twins cannot fit, stop and ask the governor for a size waiver before going over (mem:governor-hold-pending-size-waiver). Never cut a case to fit.

VERIFY ONCE (load verification-before-completion).

Run on a snapshot of HEAD plus this task's files, never against the shared checkout's live wrappers, which peers edit (mem:gotcha-shared-tree-long-harness-needs-snapshot, mem:gotcha-gate-hermetic-snapshot-from-wsl).

1. GATE: this is complete_task's verification. Run fresh; it must exit 0:
   bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh
2. Windows seat (DoD 2), per mem:gotcha-qa-windows-launcher-tests-from-wsl:
   - `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1` and `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1` pass every case;
   - `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell` and `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs pwsh` pass.
3. Held-out check: `git diff --quiet <WT-08T landed sha> -- scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1`.
4. DoD 3 grep over the worktree arm of both wrappers:
   - no --force, '-f ', --force-with-lease or '+' refspec on any push;
   - neither MOE_PUSH_REBASE nor push_branch / Push-MoeBranch is reachable from it.
5. Code parity: this diff must be empty:
   diff <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD|PUSH)_[A-Z_]+' scripts/moe-agent.sh | sort -u) <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD|PUSH)_[A-Z_]+' scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | sort -u)
6. Size: git diff --numstat over the five owned paths totals at most 380 net. Every other dirty path belongs to a peer; name it and leave it untouched.

Record the per-case pass lists for bash, PS5.1 and PS7 in the step note.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once (load adversarial-self-review). Replay QA's race and the doc's error table against the code.

Ref safety:
- Can any path move the local target to a commit the remote is not known to hold: a failed or unknown push, a fetch failure, a rejected push?
- Can any path push with force or call push_branch?

Race: two seats land in remote mode at once, with no gate.
- Does exactly one of them publish per round?
- Does the loser start a new round on '!'?
- Does a seat whose fetches all fail publish nothing, and never report DIVERGED?

Unknown outcome:
- No completion row and no finalize.
- The journal is kept with 'push unknown:', and a push-unknown rescue ref exists.
- The next pre-flight's replay fetches first and closes landed only when C is contained.

Divergence: L is read before the fetch, so a peer's mirror between your L read and your fetch cannot fake DIVERGED.

Edge inputs:
- MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC set to garbage;
- a target name with unusual characters;
- origin missing while another remote exists: remote mode, and the fetch fails closed;
- a porcelain line for another ref;
- a '+' flag;
- a failing pre-push hook.

Shared mode stays byte-identical (rail 4): postflight-safe passes unchanged.

Rails: error handling on every git call, tests present, no force push, sh/ps1 parity, and nothing under .moe written from W.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Contract correction from the WT-S revision after QA reject 1. Where this comment and the row's description differ, the revised docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md and this comment win.

WITHDRAWN, because QA reproduced a local/remote fork with them:
- "local equal to or ahead: B = local";
- "a fetch failure prints MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and B = local";
- "a transport failure … continues to the local CAS".

Plan against revised §1.2, §2.2 (L4/L9/L10), §2.3 and §2.6:
- L4 (sync_land_target / Sync-MoeLandTarget):
  - Fetch with `git fetch --no-write-fetch-head origin refs/heads/<target>:refs/remotes/origin/<target>` (no `+`), up to 3 tries, MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC apart (default 5).
  - B = refs/remotes/origin/<target>, never the local target.
  - If all 3 fetches fail, nothing lands: MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED, unlanded `remote`.
  - A local target that is not an ancestor of B gives MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED. Otherwise fast-forward the local target to B.
  - W creation (WT-04) cuts from refs/remotes/origin/<target> after this fetch. If the fetch fails it uses the ref as last fetched; with no such ref at all it gives MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- L9: `git push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/<target>`, with no force flag of any kind.
  - Flag ' ', '*' or '=': published.
  - Flag '!': the round ends.
  - Anything else goes to reconcile_push / Resolve-MoePushOutcome. It waits the backoff, then repeats the fetch:
    - C contained: published.
    - fetched without C: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, and the round ends.
    - the fetch fails: the outcome is unknown.
- Unknown outcome:
  - MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and no ref moves;
  - keep the journal, with pushResult `push unknown: <detail>`;
  - put a `push-unknown` rescue ref on C;
  - send no completion row and no finalize.
- L10 mirror: an ff-only CAS of the local target to C. A refusal is MOE_LAND_MIRROR_SKIPPED and never a landing failure.
- Worktree arm of receipt_replay / Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay: fetch first, then run the unchanged receipt_landed_as against refs/remotes/origin/<target>. A failed fetch keeps the journal; it never drops it.
- `pushed: true` only after a confirmed publication.
- Exhausted rounds end as `contention`, or as `remote` when the last round ended on a transport failure.

WT-08T's `remote` cases, including the race and the unknown outcome, must pass unchanged.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Follow-up to the WT-S revision comment above. Two additions from revised §2.2 L4 and its error handling:

1. Read the local target as L BEFORE the fetch.
   - Report MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED only when that L is not an ancestor of B.
   - Why: mirrors only ever move the local target to commits the remote already held. Read this way, a peer's mirror that lands between your fetch and your check cannot fake a divergence. That matters because no lease runs when no qualityGate is set.
   - A fetch refused as non-fast-forward counts as one failed try. When a peer moved the tracking ref mid-fetch, the next try clears it.

2. Test the remote-mode W base in scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1}, since the WT-08T files stay held out.
   - W is cut from refs/remotes/origin/<target>.
   - With no such ref, expect MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
   - This row's files become 5: the two wrappers, both postflight harnesses and .github/workflows/ci.yml.

Also extend your parity grep to cover `MOE_PUSH_`.

comments.author: architect-6fc3dd5c
comments.content:
Seams WT-08T's held-out suite relies on (task-c12f9463, plan rev 1). WT-09 must pass that suite's `remote` cases unchanged, so please plan these in:
- S1. MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF fires once per landing, after L8's journal and before L9's push. push-rejected-retry uses it to push a peer commit first, so the first push gets `!`.
- S2. L8 writes the journal on every worktree completion, at <git common dir>/moe/receipt/<taskId>.json, with receipt_report's fields. While the outcome is unknown, pushResult is `push unknown: <detail>`.
- S3. Fetch and push must resolve `git` through PATH. In ps1 that means bare `git` via PowerShell command resolution: never git.exe by absolute path, and never via cmd or node. The suite puts a shim first on PATH: a bash `git`, or `git.ps1` on Windows, which PS 5.1 resolves ahead of git.exe, verified 2026-10-30. The shim can fail fetch, fail push, or apply a push and then report failure. It logs every argv, which is how the force-flag check and the "push before the local main moves" order check work.
- The suite sets MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC=0, so please honour that env (§2.2 L4/§2.6).
- S4. pushed:true only on remote proof. A completion row is committed with sha C and ref refs/heads/main. finalize_attempt is landed with C.
- The unknown case expects no completion row and no finalize at all. A second run with an idle claim lets receipt_replay fetch, find C, mirror local main and close the attempt landed, which matches your msg-b6ea9c97 scope.
- S5. Log codes: MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED, MOE_PUSH_FAILED, MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED, and `MOE_RESCUE_REF ... sha=<C> reason=push-unknown`. The suite never asserts the finalize `unlanded` call (WT-11).
The six cases follow this row's WT-S comment cases 1-6, plus push-first-no-force.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Spike self-review correction (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 L9, §2.3, §2.6; section numbers unchanged). Where this differs from the description or comment c837807a, this comment wins.

1. L9 classification, on the target's porcelain line:
   - ` `, `*` or `=`: published.
   - `!` with `[rejected]`: the round ends.
   - `!` with `[remote rejected]`: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded `remote`, no more rounds.
   - Anything else (`[remote failure]`, a transport error, no line): reconcile_push.
2. reconcile_push / Resolve-MoePushOutcome: wait MOE_LAND_NET_BACKOFF_SEC, then repeat L4's fetch.
   - The tip contains C: published; continue at L10.
   - The tip is neither B nor contains C: C can never apply, because the remote takes C only as a fast-forward from B and the target never moves backwards (rail 1). MOE_PUSH_FAILED, and the round ends.
   - The tip is still B: push the SAME C again, then fetch again, up to 3 pushes in all. A repeat's refusal decides nothing; only the fetch does.
   - The fetch fails, or the tip is still B after the third push: unknown. Print MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, keep the journal, put C on a `push-unknown` rescue ref, and leave the attempt finalizing.
3. receipt_replay's worktree arm, in remote mode, never merges, gates or builds a commit. "Re-run L4-L12" is dropped. It settles the journaled C with reconcile_push:
   - Published: the L10 mirror, then the landed rows as today.
   - Never applies: hand off to the unlanded route with reason `remote`, through WT-11's take_unlanded_route. Until WT-11 lands, print MOE_PUSH_FAILED and drop the journal, as today's "ref never moved" path does.
   - Unknown: keep the journal for the next pre-flight.
4. Journals now exist for every completion, with `candidateId: null` when there is no gate (WT-08), so the remote arm must accept them too.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
In worktree remote mode, a completion lands only by a non-forced `git push --porcelain origin C:refs/heads/<target>` of a commit whose only parent is B = refs/remotes/origin/<target>, freshly fetched.
- The local target is a mirror. It moves only to commits the remote is known to hold.
- A rejected push starts a new round.
- An ambiguous push is reconciled by a fetch. If that fetch fails, the outcome is unknown: no ref moves, there is no completion row and no finalize, the journal is kept and a push-unknown rescue ref is made, and replay closes it later.
- W is cut from the remote-tracking target.
- Local mode and shared mode are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: All WT-08T worktree-landing cases, local and remote, pass on bash, PS5.1 and PS7 with the held-out files unchanged.
Only a confirmed publication sends pushed: true, and local mode sends pushed: false.
No push in the worktree arm carries a force flag or a '+' refspec, and MOE_PUSH_REBASE and push_branch / Push-MoeBranch are unreachable from it.
The W base in remote mode is refs/remotes/origin/<target>. With no such ref, creation fails with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED. Both cases are proven in postflight.{sh,ps1}.

ci.yml runs worktree-landing.sh on Linux and worktree-landing.ps1 on both Windows PowerShell engines. postflight-safe and parity-check pass, and the MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_, MOE_BOARD_ and MOE_PUSH_ code sets are equal across the twins.
invariants: main (the target) moves only by an update-ref CAS or a non-forced push, never by a force push or a history rewrite (epic rail 1).
No failed, rejected or unknown push ever moves the local target.
Shared-checkout mode and its push_branch behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged (rail 4).
W never contains or writes .moe runtime (rail 3).
compatibility: An existing receipt journal without the new optional field replays exactly as today.
finalize_attempt outcomes are not extended here; the unlanded route is WT-11's.
checkRefs: bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Planned now, ahead of WT-08 (the human moved the row to PLANNING). Every predecessor interface comes from the revised doc's Assumed interfaces. The worker reads WT-08's landed bytes first and extends that round loop; it does not rebuild one.
- The §2.6 re-run of L4-L12, for a still-finalizing attempt whose C is absent, goes to WT-11 (comment-c2d608e0 on task-dd1ee586). It is a resume-in-W landing that hits the owner guard and the finalizing holds, which WT-11 already designs.
- MOE_PUSH_REBASE: proven inert by a grep (DoD 3 allows a case or a grep), which saves LOC.
- Journal marker: one optional field instead of inferring the mode from the target. A journal without the field keeps today's replay arm (rail 4).
planningNotes.risks:
- WT-08's shape is unknown at plan time. If its round loop or interim failure path differs from the doc, the worker must call moe.request_replan rather than invent around it.
- Size: two language twins against a 400-net cap that counts tests. The budget is 380.
- WT-08T's shim intercepts git through PATH, so an absolute git path breaks the tests.
- A porcelain line must be matched on its destination ref, and git's exit code ignored for classification.
- An unknown outcome must leave the attempt finalizing, with no finalize at all, before and after WT-11.
